title: Efficient Magic State Factory Via Transversal Non-Clifford Gate
authors: I-Chi Chen, Hrushikesh Pramod Patil, Huiyang Zhou, Andrew Sornborger
abstract: Magic-state preparation is a central component of fault-tolerant quantum computing. Recent theoretical and experimental successes in code-switch-based magic-state preparation have underscored the promise of these methods for quantum error correction. Similarly, magic-state cultivation has likewise been demonstrated in both numerical and experimental settings. However, a thorough comparison between magic-state cultivation and code-switch-based magic-state factories is still missing. In this work, we carry out end-to-end simulations of magic-state preparation using code switching and compare its resource requirements and performance against magic-state cultivation. As part of this analysis, we develop a lattice-surgery protocol for transfer between the doubled color code and the rotated surface code. We extend the complete code-switching protocol to the $d=5$ doubled color code and perform the corresponding end-to-end simulations. Finally, we propose two fault-tolerant magic-state preparation protocols that combine phase-kickback checks with a transversal non-Clifford gate.
summary: This paper develops and compares advanced protocols for generating magic states necessary for fault-tolerant quantum computing. It integrates code switching and lattice surgery to transfer logical information between different QEC codes like color and surface codes. The results propose optimized methods that improve fidelity and reduce resource overhead compared to existing techniques.
main_problem: The work aims to thoroughly compare the resource requirements and performance between two methods for generating magic states: code-switch-based factories versus direct magic-state cultivation.
main_result: Two new fault-tolerant protocols combining phase-kickback checks with a transversal non-Clifford gate were proposed, showing consistent performance across different noise models and code distances.
method: The study uses end-to-end simulations of the entire magic-state preparation process, involving lattice surgery (LS) to transfer state information between various Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes like color codes and surface codes.
model_or_system: The research focuses on fault-tolerant quantum computation using multiple QEC codes, including the 2D/3D color code, rotated surface code, and tetrahedral code. The protocols are designed to generate logical magic states ($T|+ angle_L$ or $S|+ angle_L$).
key_observables: Logical infidelity, success rate of magic-state preparation, and the expected space-time volume per successful shot (V).
important_parameters: Physical gate error rates ($\epsilon$), code distances ($d=3, d=5$), and noise models (with/without idling noise).
main_assumptions: The analysis often approximates noisy circuits due to large qubit counts and sometimes uses $S|+ angle_L$ as a proxy for the non-Clifford $T|+ angle_L$ state preparation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow of end-to-end magic state preparation using code switching, comparing logical infidelity vs. noise strength across different dimensions and protocols.
paper_structure: The paper develops new combined protocols by integrating transversal non-Clifford gates with established techniques like code switching (CS) and lattice surgery (LS), culminating in detailed performance comparisons across various error regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, resource-aware benchmarks for implementing universal quantum computation primitives (magic states) using state-of-the-art QEC structures, which is crucial for scaling up any physical quantum hardware platform.
